<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is safe to process with `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. These commands source the PKGBUILD's top-level scope and execute `pkgver()` if present, but in this file, there is no `pkgver()` function. The only dynamic operations occur within the `build()` and `package()` functions, which are not executed under the current flags.

The `source` array uses a standard HTTPS URL pointing to the project's own GitHub release archive (`https://github.com/jpietek/PenguinBurner/archive/refs/tags/v${pkgver}.tar.gz`). This is a common and expected pattern for AUR packages. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry means the downloaded archive will not be verified — while this reduces trust in the integrity of the source, it does **not** make the sourcing or fetching step dangerous by itself. Extraction of unverified sources is part of the intended workflow for auditing; no code execution occurs during this phase due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`.

There are no command substitutions, remote code evaluations (e.g., `$(curl ...)`, `eval`), or data exfiltration attempts in the global scope. All variables and logic are static or confined to later build stages that are explicitly disabled here. Thus, simply sourcing this PKGBUILD poses no risk of unintended execution or leakage.
</details>
